verdict.rationale: Secureframe documents a Custom Integrations capability for creating and mapping custom resources from tools it has no native integration for. Raw data can be pushed to an API endpoint and Secureframe then normalizes, maps and tests it. This is backed by a published REST API reference with an embedded OpenAPI 3.0 spec and a dated versioning policy. missing for 10: evidence that externally computed test results (not just raw resource data) can be pushed directly, documentation of the specific custom-resource ingestion endpoints in the reference, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build private/custom integrations against a documented API to push evidence and test results from systems the catalog doesn't cover

citations.quote: Custom Integrations, which enables you to create and map custom resources from tools and services that Secureframe doesn't offer a native integration with.
Ingest data from cloud, on-prem, hybrid, or legacy systems and even custom-built tools. Push raw data via an API endpoint or CSV upload
Push raw data via an API endpoint or CSV upload and let Secureframe handle normalization, mapping, and testing for compliance-related resources
Secureframe exposes a REST API for use by customers, partners, and community developers.
Backwards _incompatible_ changes require Secureframe to release a new dated API version
